lines.trans: Salt the meat exactly in seven minutes.
Then our meat will be much more tender.
Understood, Chef, I am clocking the exact time.
Step aside a little, do not disturb me!
Excuse me, Chef, I am simply watching carefully.
Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.
Yes, Chef, I am not stepping away anywhere!
The main thing is do not overcook this tender fillet.
I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.
Serve the meat to the guests on a hot plate.
It will be executed in the very best form!

words.gram: short passive past participle, neuter singular

Then our meat will be much more tender.

Then our meat will be much more tender.
Understood, Chef, I am clocking the exact time.

words.gram: short passive past participle, neuter singular

lines.trans: Salt the meat exactly in seven minutes.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: иметь в виду = to mean, to have in mind
иметь в виду = to mean, to have in mind

examples.trans: What do you mean?

examples.text: Из окна красивый вид на парк.
examples.trans: There is a nice view of the park from the window.

examples.text: Что вы имеете в виду, Клавдия Викторовна?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Klavdia Viktorovna?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Read everything carefully!
Listen to the teacher attentively.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'on time'.

examples.trans: Bad timing!
He always comes on time.

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I don't have time.
We're having a good time.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.
You have visitors!

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'readiness'.
Secondary conversational sense ('willingness') (eagerness to act) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.

examples.text: Повар проверяет готовность мяса специальным термометром.
examples.trans: The cook checks the doneness of the meat with a special thermometer.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.en: to time, to start the clock
meanings.note: засекать время; Засекай! = Time me!
Secondary conversational sense ('to spot, to notice') (colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm timing it.

examples.text: Понял, шеф, я засекаю точное время.
examples.trans: Understood, Chef, I am clocking the exact time.

examples.text: Давай засекай ровно три минуты, я начинаю жарить стейк!
examples.trans: Go ahead and time exactly three minutes, I am starting to fry the steak!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to excuse, to forgive') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Sorry, please.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'полнить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to execute', forming an aspectual pair with 'исполнять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to perform') (to perform on stage) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Будет исполнено в самом лучшем виде!
examples.trans: It will be executed in the very best form!

examples.text: Ваше желание будет исполнено в самом лучшем виде!
examples.trans: Your wish will be fulfilled in the very best way!

examples.text: Шеф приказал немедленно исполнить заказ важного гостя.
examples.trans: The chef ordered to immediately fulfill the important guest's order.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is the best day!
You're my best friend.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

мешать.gloss: to be in the way, to disturb

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be in the way', forming an aspectual pair with 'помешать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to disturb, to bother') (Не мешай! = Don't bother me!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The radiators are in the way.
Don't bother me!

examples.text: Филиппыч, миксер проехать не может. Радиаторы мешают.
examples.trans: Filippych, the mixer truck can't get through. The radiators are in the way.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'meat', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?
Very tasty meat!

examples.text: И мой тоже готов! А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: And mine is ready too! Where do you get your meat?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: much, far, a lot (before a comparative)
meanings.note: намного хуже = much worse; намного лучше = much better

examples.trans: In prison it will be much worse.
Today is much warmer.

examples.text: Но я же вижу, как тебе плохо. В тюрьме будет намного хуже, поверь мне.
examples.trans: But I can see how bad things are for you. In prison it will be much worse, believe me.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'жный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('gentle, tender, delicate').

examples.text: Я могу быть очень нежным и ласковым.
examples.trans: I can be very gentle and affectionate.

examples.text: Марина, я могу быть очень нежным и ласковым.
examples.trans: Marina, I can be very gentle and affectionate.

examples.text: Тогда наше мясо будет намного нежнее.
examples.trans: Then our meat will be much more tender.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: contrast нигде = nowhere (location)

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.
I wasn't hiding anywhere!

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'fire', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I open return fire!

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Срочно снимай сковороду с горячего огня!
examples.trans: Urgently take the pan off the hot fire!

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left
Secondary conversational sense ('to stay') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ойти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to step back', forming an aspectual pair with 'отходить'.

examples.trans: Step back from the car!
He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to step away', forming an aspectual pair with 'отойти'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to leave') (to depart from a place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Да, шеф, я не отхожу никуда!
examples.trans: Yes, Chef, I am not stepping away anywhere!

examples.text: Да, шеф, я ни на шаг не отхожу от плиты!
examples.trans: Yes, Chef, I am not stepping away from the stove by a single step!

examples.text: Не отходи далеко от раздачи, сейчас пойдут горячие заказы.
examples.trans: Do not step far from the pass, hot orders are about to start coming.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'жарить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to overcook', forming an aspectual pair with 'пережаривать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to overfry') (to brown excessively) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Главное, не пережарь это нежное филе.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not overcook this tender fillet.

examples.text: Главное — ни в коем случае не пережарь это нежное филе.
examples.trans: The main thing is under no circumstances to overcook this tender fillet.

examples.text: Если пережарить утиную грудку, мясо станет слишком сухим.
examples.trans: If you overfry the duck breast, the meat will become too dry.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stove', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('slab') (large flat stone or concrete block) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно смотри за температурой на плите.
examples.trans: Watch carefully the temperature on the stove.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Ладно, включай плиту и доставай мясо!
examples.trans: All right, turn on the stove and get the meat!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'авать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to serve'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to serve, hand') (food or items) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Как будто ты подаёшь на развод.
examples.trans: As if you are filing for divorce.

examples.text: Подавай мясо на горячей тарелке гостям.
examples.trans: Serve the meat to the guests on a hot plate.

examples.text: Вика, скорее подавай гостям горячие блюда!
examples.trans: Vika, serve the hot dishes to the guests quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I didn't understand.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
examples.trans: Did you definitely understand how to slice this steak properly?

проследить.gloss: to see to it, to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to keep an eye on, to make sure
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'следить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to see to it', forming an aspectual pair with 'следить'.

examples.trans: We'll keep an eye on it.
I'll keep an eye on the children.
All right. My students and I will keep an eye on it.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Secondary conversational sense ('evenly, smoothly') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Exactly ten seconds.
Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('seven') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.trans: Not eight years, but seven.
Seven days in a week.

examples.text: Там депозит на семь тысяч рублей!
examples.trans: There's a deposit for seven thousand roubles!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'frying pan', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('skillet') (shallow cooking pan) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Рыба почти готова на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: The fish is almost ready on the hot pan.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch') (TV, a film) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Look what I've got.
I'm watching TV.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

снять.gloss: to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent

meanings.en: to film, to take a photo/video of
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to film', forming an aspectual pair with 'снимать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to take off, to remove') (clothing) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('to rent') (a flat or room) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон.
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone.
He took off his coat by the door.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон. И сразу все мне помогают!
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone. And right away everyone helps me!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'олить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to salt', forming an aspectual pair with 'посолить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to cure') (to preserve with salt) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Соли мясо ровно через семь минут.
examples.trans: Salt the meat exactly in seven minutes.

examples.text: Соли горячее мясо ровно через семь минут после жарки.
examples.trans: Salt the hot meat exactly seven minutes into frying.

examples.text: Шеф никогда не разрешает солить блюдо, не попробовав его.
examples.trans: The chef never allows salting a dish without tasting it first.

meanings.note: с другой стороны = on the other hand
Secondary conversational sense ('direction') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'plate'.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.
Put clean plates on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Back then I was little.
Then come tomorrow.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('exact, precise').

examples.trans: An exact answer.
Nobody knows the exact answer.
Wait, is this information accurate at all?

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('three') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.trans: Three days.
I have three sons.
We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'fillet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('tenderloin') (choice tender meat cut) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Главное, не пережарь это нежное филе.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not overcook this tender fillet.

examples.text: Сначала удалить хребет и охладить филе?
examples.trans: First remove the backbone and chill the fillet?

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week
Secondary conversational sense ('through, across') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll come in an hour.
In a week.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
